# Demo Episode: Retention Frameworks and Sustainable Growth Loops

> [!NOTE]
> Disclaimer: This document contains synthesized demo excerpts for educational and testing purposes within The Lenny Growth Assistant.

## Why Retention Is the Foundation of Growth

Retention is the single most important metric for any recurring business. If your retention curve does not flatten parallel to the x-axis, your product is a leaky bucket, and pouring acquisition dollars into it will inevitably lead to growth plateaus.

A flattening retention curve proves that a core cohort of users continues to find value over months and years. For consumer social products, a flat line at 15-25% monthly active user retention is good; for enterprise SaaS, net revenue retention (NRR) should be well over 100% to 120%, while user-level logo retention should flatten around 70-85%.

## Moving Away From Linear Funnels to Compounding Loops

Traditional marketing thinks in terms of linear funnels: Awareness -> Acquisition -> Activation -> Retention -> Referral -> Revenue. Funnels have a fundamental flaw: you have to keep feeding more inputs at the top to get more outputs at the bottom.

In contrast, sustainable growth engines are built around Growth Loops. A growth loop is a closed system where the actions of one cohort of users naturally generate inputs for the next cohort of users:

1. Viral / Word-of-Mouth Loops: A user collaborates with a colleague (like Figma or Slack), exposing the colleague to the product.
2. Content / SEO Loops: Users create public artifacts (like Notion templates, Pinterest boards, or Yelp reviews) that get indexed by search engines and attract organic searchers.
3. Paid Acquisition Reinvestment Loops: Monetized users generate revenue that is directly reinvested into paid advertising to acquire new cohorts profitably.

## Leading Indicators of Churn

Do not wait for cancellation to diagnose churn. Leading indicators include:
- Drop in natural usage frequency (e.g., dropping from 4 logins/week to 1 login/week).
- Decrease in feature breadth (e.g., stopping the use of integrations or exports).
- Departures of key internal product champions in B2B accounts.
